newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev closes firmer at 1,525-1,530 per dlr.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev closes firmer at 1,525-1,530 per dlr.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 1,525-1,530 to the dollar, up from 1,555-1,560 at midday and the opening's 1,565-1,570, dealers said.
"The lev gained some 40 per dollar on the day as (dollar) demand from clients was almost nil and the central bank was also not seen buying foreign currency," a bank dealer said.
Central bank officials were not available for comment.
Traders expected movements in the exchange rate next week to again depend on the central bank, which has been seen as the main dollar buyer since February.
"The lev will probably rise further next week unless the central bank bids for dollars as foreign currency demand from clients is expected to remain low," another dealer said.

The central bank was a a net foreign currency buyer in the past two months, boosting its reserves by around $110 million to $554.3 million at end-March ahead of the planned introduction of a fixed exchange rate mechanism in June.

Under the mechanism, called a currency board system, levs in circulation must be matched by central bank reserves, which would curb the financial powers of the government and the central bank and prevent the printing of money. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
